categories.name: credential_access
categories.description: Harvesting and reusing valid credentials across Subnet 1 to reach the dual-homed host (Valid Accounts, T0859).
hints: VM1/1c/1d/1e share a cloned golden image. Check for a single local admin account reused across every host on Subnet 1 before trying anything fancier (Kerberoasting/GPO abuse are not relevant here).
Dump local credentials from the foothold host (e.g. LSASS, SAM) and try the same local admin account against the other hosts on 10.1.1.0/24 over SMB/WinRM.

The local admin account name/password is identical on VM1, VM1c, VM1d and VM1e. Finding it once and reusing it via PsExec/WinRM against each host in turn gets you onto all of them, including the dual-homed host (VM2).

categories.name: recon_ot_enumeration
categories.description: Finding the OT network from the dual-homed host and enumerating its device population (T0840/T0846/T0888).
hints: Once on the dual-homed host, check its network interfaces — one of them reaches a second network you haven't seen from Subnet 1.
That second interface puts you on 10.1.3.0/24. Scan it for hosts speaking IEC 61850 MMS (TCP port 102); you'll find more than one.

Three hosts on 10.1.3.0/24 speak MMS: 10.1.3.1, 10.1.3.50 and 10.1.3.51. Query GetServerDirectory/GetLogicalDeviceDirectory on each — the real breaker-control relay is the one exposing a genuine XCBR logical node, not just any device that answers.

categories.name: decoy_avoidance
categories.description: Distinguishing the real relay from the two simulator decoys by protocol-level inspection, not by guessing.
hints: Not every device on the OT network is the one you want. Compare their IEC 61850 data models structurally before issuing any control command.
A device missing an XCBR logical node entirely, or exposing a misleading model identifier, is not the breaker-control relay — rule those out first.

Confirm the real device by its logical device name and the presence of a genuine XCBR node under proper IEC 61850 semantics before sending Select/Operate; an incorrect target is a discoverable, logged trap, not a scenario-ending event.
